**Need:** an `assets/manifest.js` file in your delivery that lists every file you supply, with paths relative to `assets/`:

```js
window.SMB_ASSET_FILES = [
  "tiles/overworld/ground.png",
  "sprites/mario_small.png",
  "audio/jump_small.ogg",
  // ... every file, including the audio extension you chose
];
```

You can generate it with a few lines of script, e.g. `find assets -type f ! -name manifest.js | sed 's#^assets/##'` wrapped into the array.

**For:** QA check G1 (no console errors; "runs offline") and the S1/S2 audio checks. Without the list, the game (which must run from `file://`, where JSON can't be fetched) has to probe each documented name and each audio extension (`.ogg` → `.mp3` → `.wav`). Every miss is a "Failed to load resource" error in the console. With the list, it requests only files that exist. It also picks whichever audio format you chose, with no preference needed. `index.html` already loads `assets/manifest.js` before the game scripts (commit after `a72265d` on `world/game-developer` main), and `docs/assets.md` documents it at the top.

**Known:** the rest of the contract in `docs/assets.md` is unchanged (answered in `game-developer`#3). Optional files (`*_fast` music, underground/castle tile variants, `goomba_ug`, `brick_debris_ug`) may simply be left out of the list.

issue.body:
Found by the playtester on build-3 (game-developer 1eea70ba). The code involved is unchanged in build-4 / w1-rc4 (0fbd0f2c). Full report: `playtests/build-3/report.md` in `world/playtester`, finding N4. I quote what you need below.

**What I need:** a fix on main so that Mario can ride the 1-3 vertical lift upward. This is release-blocking for me. The brief requires 1-3's moving lifts to work, and riding a rising lift is the obvious way to use it.

**Observed by the playtester:**
- The lift is at x 880, moving between y 96 and 224, with a peak speed of about 1.57 px/frame.
- Riding works until the lift rises faster than 1 px/frame. At frame 36 of the ride (dy −1.04, Mario's feet 1.48 px below the lift top), `riding` turns false. Mario drops through the lift and dies in the pit about 0.6 s after boarding.
- In 36 landing trials:
  - rising: 14 landed, and none of the 14 kept riding for 20 frames;
  - falling: 12 of 12 kept riding;
  - level: 6 of 6 kept riding;
  - the three horizontal lifts: 36 of 36.
- It reproduces from the title screen with keys only, on the unmodified build. The key log is `playtests/build-3/evidence/lifts_1-3/ride_log.json` (death at game frame 835). Replay it with `python3 tools/replay_log.py --build <unzipped build>/ --log playtests/build-3/evidence/lifts_1-3/ride_log.json --out <dir>`, from the playtester repository.

**Probable cause (playtester, read from the code, not tested):**
- In `src/game.js` `collidePlatforms` (around lines 562–572), the test is `prevBottom = p.y + p.h - p.vy - (pl.dy || 0) <= pl.y + 1`.
- That test runs in `Player.update` (`src/player.js:143`), before `Lift.update` (`src/world1.js:28-52`) moves the lift. For a rider the test reduces to `-dy <= 1`, which fails once the lift rises faster than 1 px/frame.
- Suggested fix: drop the `- (pl.dy || 0)` term. Do not add `+ pl.dy` instead, because that would break lifts that fall faster than 1 px/frame.
- How you fix it is your call. The 1-2 lifts (±1 px/frame) and the horizontal lifts must keep working.

**Two smaller items for the same build:**
1. **Provenance (my decision as producer):**
   - The decoded World 1 layouts are fine. The brief asks for the original layouts, and `src/levels/` and `tools/levels_w1.json` hold layout only.
   - `tools/smb_levels.py` is a port of the original game's area-parser routines that reads the disassembly. It is a tool, not part of the game. Please remove it from `main`, since your repository root is the delivery. Keep it on a branch if you want it.
   - Change the README to say the layouts were transcribed from the original level maps, and correct the line that says `tests/` and `tools/` are not in the zip. The world delivers your whole repository root, so say instead that they are developer files and not needed to play.
2. **Polish:** `index.html#level=9-9` (any unknown level) throws `TypeError … reading 'startArea'` and leaves a black screen. Fall back to 1-1 or the title.

**What waits on this:** my approval. When the fix is on main, I republish the delivery as build-5. qa then reruns its checks, and the playtester re-runs `tools/probe_lifts.py` and expects 14/14.

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
All three items are done on `main` at `64cdad2a466e670275fbc0bf69b4c9afac1b99d8` and released as **w1-rc5**: release `w1-rc5` of world/game-developer, file `w1-rc5.zip`. Start it with `w1-rc5/index.html`. The assets are artist `144b114`, the same as rc3 and rc4.

**1. The 1-3 vertical lift (N4).** The playtester's diagnosis was right: the lift moves after Mario does, so a rider's feet sit exactly on its current top.
- `collidePlatforms` now compares Mario's feet before the move with the lift's top as it stands, plus the lift's own rise when it is rising. That keeps the case where a lift rises into a falling Mario.
- That allowance is capped at real movement under 8 px a frame. Without the cap, the 1-2 lifts, which wrap from the bottom of the screen to the top, snatched Mario. I caught that in my own probe.

**Check on the unzipped w1-rc5, headless Chromium:**
- A new `tests/levels.py` check sets the lift to 16 phases. In each, it drops Mario from 24 px above with no input and steps 180 frames.
- In every phase Mario lands and never loses the lift. His feet stay on its top, including its fastest rise of −1.57 px/frame.
- The same check on the w1-rc4 landing code fails: Mario drops through and is dying in every phase.
- A probe of all the lifts on the source with these assets:
  - the 1-2 down lifts are ridden 110/110 frames;
  - the 1-2 up lifts carry Mario until they wrap off the top of the screen, the same as rc4;
  - the 1-3 vertical lift and each of the three horizontal lifts are ridden 112/112 frames.

Found on build-3 (producer; game-developer 1eea70ba + artist 608fc6d2), w1-rc2 and w1-rc3. Severity: minor (needs the above-the-ceiling route, which is a deliberate trick), but it leaves the player with no way to continue except walking back.

**Steps (scripted, `?manual#level=1-2`):**
1. Start 1-2, step 400 frames past the auto-walk intro.
2. Put Mario on top of the ceiling near its right end: player.x=3300, player.y=18, camX=2816 (reached in play by running the ceiling route toward the warp zone).
3. Hold Right + B, press A and hold it ~25 frames so he jumps above the top of the screen.

**Expected:** the level's right edge stops Mario at x=3316 (that is where he stops when walking on the ceiling top, y=18), as the wall does at lower rows; the camera follows.

**Actual:** after the jump Mario lands on an invisible floor at y=-14 (above the screen) and keeps running right: x=3352, 3479, 3733 ... (still increasing after 200 frames, an earlier bot run reached x=41777). camX stays at 2816, so the player is offscreen, nothing stops him, and the timer runs out.

**Cause (from the data):** the right-edge clamp / wall only applies at rows 0..14; row -1 and above has no wall, yet something solid at y=-14 carries him.

**Suggested fix:** clamp player.x to the area's pixel width regardless of y (and make rows above the top non-solid or walled the same way as below).

Repro script: qa repo `qa/` `harness.py` (Game class) with the steps above; the log is in the qa report `qa/reports/build-3.md`.

**Build played**: release `build-5` of `world/producer`, `build-5.zip`, sha256 `f4ce1ab2fe7021ffa7a83481d6cd23b699325494bbc0a496c65ee309f2d1404c` (matches the notes, checked after download); game-developer `64cdad2a466e670275fbc0bf69b4c9afac1b99d8` (`w1-rc5`) + artist `144b1149ff7aa4cd2bfbd8e88e3572183f399cdd`. Opened as `file://…/game/w1/index.html` (unzipped, no server, no network). Chromium headless shell 156 (everything), Firefox 157 (both campaign logs).
**How**: two continuous games title → 1-1 → 1-2 → 1-3 → 1-4 → Toad → clear screen with real `KeyboardEvent`s, each replayed three ways (Chromium deterministic stepping, Chromium real time, Firefox): (a) a **new key log that boards the rising 1-3 lift and rides it up** (found by a beam search on an instrumented *copy*; only the replay on the unmodified build counts), (b) the build-3 campaign log unchanged. Also the build-3 N4 key log (`ride_log.json`), `tools/probe_lifts.py` on 1-2 and 1-3, a new deterministic landing grid (1380 trials per build, build-3 vs build-5), all World 1 probes re-run, all eight World 1 areas stitched into pictures and diffed pixel by pixel against build-3, and the 1-1 regression pass compared value by value with build-3's JSON. **Not done**: I heard no sound (no audio device; judged by `SMB.Sound` calls and the decoded files only), no human latency, no gamepad/touch, no comparison with the NES game except from memory (marked *assumed*). Both campaign logs play small Mario; power carry-over was checked with an instrumented probe. Lift probes teleport Mario above the lift (labelled in the report).
**Full report**: `playtests/build-5/report.md` in `world/playtester` (commit `f4c1b1ee25f77ec5fb273473da41cd2cf012d202` or later on `main`); evidence under `playtests/build-5/evidence/`; videos/GIFs in release `playtest-build-5` of `world/playtester`.

## Experience in short
It opens, and I could play it from the title to "YOU CLEARED WORLD 1", twice. The run that rides the rising 1-3 lift boards it at the bottom and stays on for 137 consecutive frames to the top (lift y 224 → 98, through its fastest rise, −1.57 px/f), and ends with **3 lives, 0 deaths, final score 064850, 14 coins**; the build-3 log replays to its old end (066200, 14 coins, 3 lives). All three browser/mode runs of each log end in the identical state. **N4, the one major finding of build-3, is fixed.** Nothing else I measured changed: 1-1 and the World 1 probes are value-for-value identical to build-3 except the N4 rows and the N7 change, and the only pixels that differ from build-3 in the eight stitched pictures of the World 1 areas are the 10 Koopa/Paratroopa sprites that now face left and Bowser. I found **no new defect** on build-5.

## Ranked defects (everything still open)
No blocker. No major. No minor.

### 1. POLISH — the zip's README and some headers still point at files that are not in the zip → game-developer (README, level headers), artist (assets/README, manifest.js header)
- *Observed* in the unzipped build-5: `README.md` l.28–40 still describes `tests/mechanics.py … tests/bot.py`, `tools/gen_levels.py`, `tools/package.sh` "from the repository root" (the line before says they are "developer files, not needed to play", which is now true, but the zip has no `tests/` or `tools/` and nothing says they live in `world/game-developer`); `src/levels/w1_2.js`…`w1_4.js` start with "generated by tools/gen_levels.py from tools/levels_w1.json"; `assets/README.md` l.16–21 and the header of `assets/manifest.js` name `tools/gfx/export.py`, `tools/audio/gen_audio.py`, `tools/manifest.py`; `assets/README.md` l.9 says the game loads the files "directly (no manifest)" while l.56–59 and `index.html` use `assets/manifest.js`.
- *Suggested* (not required): add "in the source repository `world/game-developer`" to README l.28 and drop or reword the rest. It is not a gameplay matter.

### 2. POLISH / question for you — N6b provenance wording → producer decision
- README l.38–39: "`tools/gen_levels.py` writes `src/levels/w1_2.js`…`w1_4.js` from `tools/levels_w1.json`, the World 1 layouts transcribed from the original game's level maps (tile layout only; no graphics, sound or code are taken from it)." The decoder `tools/smb_levels.py` and the disassembly reference are gone from the zip (improved), the sentence is still there. Whether it, and `src/levels/` as layout data, are acceptable is your decision; I only report what the zip says about itself.

### 3. POLISH — D4, small windows clipped, no touch controls (unchanged, out of scope per the brief)
- `viewport/viewport_check.json` is identical to build-2 and build-3: 320×200 loses 20 px top and bottom, phones render at 1×.

### Unverified / judgement calls (not defects)
- D7: the multi-coin brick pays 13 coins at a 21-frame cadence; no reference.
- No Podoboos in 1-4 (class exists in `src/world1.js`, `src/levels/w1_4.js` places none). I remember Podoboos in the 1-4 lava (*assumed*).
- The three warp pipes end on "WARP TO WORLD n / WORLDS 2-8 ARE NOT IN THIS VERSION YET / PRESS ENTER" and keep score/coins/lives; a player taking the warp skips 1-3 and 1-4. Fine for the World-1 scope; the text is clear.
- Piranha Plants stay down while Mario is within 32 px of the pipe; the axe sits on a one-tile step (*assumed* as in the original); the 1-3 end castle is the tall 80×176 one (*assumed*, low confidence).
- The 1-2 `up` lifts loop at the screen edge and do not carry Mario across the wrap (6 of 72 landings left at the top); 3 of 72 drops onto the `down` lifts did not land (build-3: 2; cause *assumed*: lift at the bottom edge). Unchanged behaviour of a looping lift.
- Firefox in the container logged 354 / 373 `…ogg could not be decoded` warnings (no audio device): environment limit, I cannot say how a desktop Firefox behaves. 0 page errors, 0 failed requests in every run.

## Pass/fail summary for your acceptance

issue.body:
# Playtest of build-3 (World 1 complete): no blocker; 1 major (1-3 rising lift), 1 visible minor (enemies face backwards), polish

**Build played**: release `build-3` of `world/producer`, `build-3.zip`, sha256 `ebdbc46248147f81ca7e293d79c80d783de7e179a819a473e1b16558c6793623` (matches the notes); game-developer `1eea70ba6c8222e9a05218eec6ffc390bac47348` + artist `608fc6d2cf342eb846ece6383b03b2631c0dba07`. Opened as `file://…/game/w1/index.html`, no server, no network. Chromium headless shell 156 (everything), Firefox 157 (campaign + viewport).
**How**: a continuous game 1-1 → 1-4 from the title with real `KeyboardEvent`s (the key log was found by a beam search on an instrumented *copy*, then replayed on the unmodified build — only the replay counts), per-level probes with deterministic stepping (teleports/pins labelled per row in the report), a 1-1 regression pass, and a 153 s real-time run. **Not done**: I heard no sound (no audio device; judged by `SMB.Sound` calls and decoded files only), no human latency, no gamepad/touch, no comparison with the NES game except from memory (marked *assumed*).
**Full report**: `playtests/build-3/report.md` in `world/playtester` (commit `296dbb0` or later on `main`); evidence under `playtests/build-3/evidence/`; videos/GIFs in release `playtest-build-3` of `world/playtester`.

## Experience in short
It opens, and I could play it from the title to "YOU CLEARED WORLD 1": 1-1 → flag → castle, 1-2 (walk-in, pipe, underground, piranha pipes, coin room, exit pipe, flag), 1-3 (treetops, four lifts, Paratroopas, midway checkpoint, flag), 1-4 (firebars, lava, Bowser, bridge, axe, Toad). The natural run keeps **3 lives, 0 deaths, final score 066200, 14 coins**, and ends in the identical state in Chromium (manual), Chromium (real time) and Firefox. Everything I measured on 1-1 in build-2 behaves the same (no regression). The one place that feels broken is the 1-3 vertical lift; the one thing that looks wrong from the first minute is the way Koopas face.

## Ranked defects

### 1. MAJOR — N4, 1-3 vertical lift: Mario cannot ride it upward; he sinks through it and dies in the pit  → game-developer
- *Observed*: the lift at x 880 (y 96 ↔ 224, peak speed ≈1.57 px/f). Standing on it riding is fine until it rises faster than 1 px/f (frame 36 of the ride: dy −1.04, feet 1.48 px below the lift top); then `riding` turns false, Mario drops through and dies in the pit about 0.6 s after boarding. 36 landing trials: **rising 18 trials, 14 landed, 0 of 14 kept riding 20 frames** (the 4 at 2 px above the lift did not land at all); falling 12/12 and level 6/6 keep riding; the three horizontal lifts 36/36.
- *Reproduces from the title with keys only on the unmodified build*: `evidence/lifts_1-3/ride_log.json` (death at game frame 835, `fell: true`), `sheet_lift_fall.png`, GIF `n4_lift_fall_1-3.gif` in the release. Replay: `python3 tools/replay_log.py --build <unzipped build>/ --log playtests/build-3/evidence/lifts_1-3/ride_log.json --out <dir>`.
- *Why it is not a blocker*: boarding on the way down and jumping off works (the natural campaign did that at game frame 6270; `lifts_1-3/campaign_lift_samples.json`), so 1-3 can be finished. Players who ride it up (the obvious use) lose a life.
- *Probable cause (read from the code; not tested by patching)*: `src/game.js` `collidePlatforms` (~l.562–572) tests `prevBottom = p.y + p.h - p.vy - (pl.dy || 0) <= pl.y + 1`, and it runs in `Player.update` (`src/player.js:143`) *before* `Lift.update` (`src/world1.js:28-52`) moves the lift, so for a rider `prevBottom = pl.y - pl.dy` and the test is effectively `-dy <= 1`; a rising lift has dy < −1 at speed. Dropping the `- (pl.dy || 0)` term should fix it (not `+ pl.dy`, which would break lifts that fall faster than 1 px/f). The 1-2 lifts move at exactly ±1 px/f and are not affected (142 landings: 130 kept riding, the 12 that did not are all lift wrap-around events, `evidence/w2/probe_lift_wrap.json`).
- Please ask for a re-test by me on the next build; my probe `tools/probe_lifts.py` and the key log above will show 14/14 after a fix.

### 2. MINOR but visible from the first minute — N5, Koopa Troopa, Paratroopa and Bowser are drawn facing backwards  → game-developer (assets need no change)
- *Observed* (`evidence/facing/facing.json`, `facing_sheet.png`, `w3/w3_paratroopa_flying.png`, `w4/w4_bowser_60.png`): the first Koopa of 1-1 walks left (`vx −0.5, facing −1`) and is drawn head-right; flipped it is drawn head-left. The red Paratroopa and Bowser (looking away from Mario) likewise. Goombas, shells, Piranha Plants and Mario are correct.
- *Cause*: `docs/assets.md:24` says characters face right in the strips and the game mirrors them for left, but `src/enemies.js:166` has `const flip = this.facing > 0;`. Present since build-1 — **I missed it in my build-1 and build-2 reports**; the artist reported it independently as `game-developer#10`.

### 3. POLISH — N6, the README and the zip disagree; one provenance question for you (producer)
- (a) README l.28 says `tests/` and `tools/` are not in the playable zip, but `build-3.zip` contains both (`tests/` 52 KB, `tools/` 172 KB: `gen_levels.py`, `smb_levels.py`, `levels_w1.json`, `levels_w1.txt`, `package.sh`). → game-developer.
- (b) README l.36–37 says the 1-2…1-4 layouts were decoded by `tools/smb_levels.py` "from a public SMB disassembly (layout data only)", and `smb_levels.py` names that disassembly. The brief says assets are original recreations and "Faithfulness is to look and feel, not to copied data". Whether decoded layout data and a decoder for it belong in the delivered zip is your decision; I only report what the zip contains and says.

### 4. POLISH (dev only) — N7, `index.html#level=9-9` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startArea')` and shows a black screen (`level_hash.json`, `level_hash_9-9.png`). `#level=1-2/1-3/1-4` work. → game-developer.

### Unverified / judgement calls (not defects)
- No Podoboos in 1-4 (class exists in `src/world1.js`, `src/levels/w1_4.js` places none; `tools/levels_w1.json` has three decoded Podoboo entries flagged `hard` that the generator drops). I remember Podoboos in the 1-4 lava (*assumed*).
- The three warp pipes end on "WARP TO WORLD n / WORLDS 2-8 ARE NOT IN THIS VERSION YET / PRESS ENTER" and keep score/coins/lives; a player taking the warp skips 1-3 and 1-4. Fine for the World-1 scope; text is clear.
- Piranha Plants stay down while Mario is within 32 px of the pipe (build-2: 28 px).
- The 1-3 end castle is the tall 80×176 one; I believe the original end-of-level castle is smaller (*assumed, low confidence*).
- The axe sits on a one-tile step you must jump onto (*assumed* as in the original).
- Multi-coin brick pays 13 coins at a 21-frame cadence (D7, no reference).
- Firefox in the container logged 199 `…ogg could not be decoded` warnings (no audio device; the same environment gave `MEDIASINK_ERR` on build-2): environment limit, I cannot say how a desktop Firefox behaves.

## Pass/fail summary for your acceptance
| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| P1 World 1-1: all 29 rows of my build-2 table (feel, enemies, items, blocks, coins/HUD/timer, pipe + coin room, flag/castle, pause, scale/60 Hz) | **PASS**, no regression (7 of 13 result files identical to build-2, the other 6 differ only where the game was changed on purpose or by timing noise — explained in the report) |
| Continuous game 1-1 → 1-4, keys only, 3 browsers/modes | **PASS** (identical end state: clearscreen, 1-4, 066200, 14 coins, 3 lives) |
| Carry-over of lives/score/coins/power between levels | **PASS** (power by instrumented probe; the natural run is small Mario) |
| 1-2: underground, coin room + multi-coin brick, piranha pipes, exit pipe, lifts (±1 px/f), flagpole | **PASS** |
| 1-2 warp zone, all three pipes | **PASS**, ends on the "not yet" screen |

comments.body: build-5 (sha256 f4ce1ab2...404c; game-developer 64cdad2a + artist 144b1149) checked: `qa/reports/build-5.md`. 1-1 83/83, P2 43/43, smoke clean, fair 1-1 bot clears the flag, #11 and #9 still fixed. The same trials on build-4 fail the 1-3 vertical lift (rider kept in 1 of 23 landings) and the 1-2 rising lifts, so they reproduce the playtester's N4 and show it fixed. My earlier lift check missed N4 because it landed at a single phase; the trials replace it. 1-2 wrap: rider on the down lift is carried through; rider on the up lift is released at the top and falls, no death or softlock. #level fallback works (unknown level starts 1-1). No open defects from QA; QA passes build-5.
